candidatos.titulo: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
candidatos.autores: Swann Bessa, Pierre-Emmanuel Mazaré, Gergely Szilvasy, Hugo Touvron, David Picard, Matthijs Douze
candidatos.resumo: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. In this paper, we introduce an exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means with mini-batch updates, powered by modern deep learning machinery and new insights. We also establish scaling laws on how decay rate and batch size impact final performance. candidatos.titulo: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training
candidatos.autores: Adia Khalid Khan, Lukas Gehring, Benjamin Paaßen
candidatos.resumo: Robustness and interpretability are interrelated and desirable properties of machine learning models. A model that changes its prediction under imperceptible perturbations behaves inconsistently with human-recognizable features and, hence, is not interpretable. Prototype-based classifiers such as Generalized Learning Vector Quantization address both at once. candidatos.titulo: MV-IVF: Multi-Vector Retrieval via Multi-Vector Clustering
candidatos.autores: Kishen N Gowda, Laxman Dhulipala, Lars Gottesbüren, Rajesh Jayaram
candidatos.resumo: Multi-vector retrieval represents each query and document as a set of embeddings and scores relevance via fine-grained set-to-set interactions such as MaxSim (Chamfer similarity). This expressiveness improves retrieval quality over single-vector representations, but makes search substantially more expensive. Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. candidatos.titulo: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
candidatos.autores: Henry Han

A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart. candidatos.autores: Daniel Salwasser, Lars Gottesbüren, Laxman Dhulipala, Jakub Łącki, Guy Blelloch, Rajesh Jayaram

candidatos.titulo: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
candidatos.autores: Kai Ponel, Marco Polignano, Erasmo Purificato, Aylin Julia Temizkan, Marco Levantesi, Giovanni Semeraro

This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. candidatos.titulo: Enabling AWS Cloud FPGA Development Using High-Level Vitis HLS
candidatos.autores: David Rostcheck
candidatos.resumo: We present a toolchain for development of ML models on AWS EC2 F2 cloud FPGA infrastructure from high-level language, implementing a complete Vitis HLS to HDK bridge to AFI workflow that has been absent from the academic literature despite eight years of AWS FPGA availability. candidatos.titulo: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation
candidatos.autores: Chang Liu, Ke Han, Niccolò Biondi, Gloria Isotton, Elisa Ricci, Davide Talon
candidatos.resumo: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation. This requires a model to decide what signs should be expressed and to realize them through precise handshape, trajectory, facial expression and body coordination. candidatos.titulo: Where Is VLA Inference Time Spent? Bottlenecks and Optimization Interactions Across GPUs
candidatos.autores: Muhammad Danish Waseem, Ahmed Ali-Eldin Hassan
candidatos.resumo: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map camera observations and language instructions to robot actions. However, their large backbones and repeated action generation can make inference take longer than the robot's real-time requirements for its next action. To reduce the load of VLA computations, researchers have proposed multiple optimization approaches, including quantization and pruning. candidatos.titulo: Item Representations Matter: Bridging Hard Semantic IDs and Soft Prototype Mixtures for Generative Retrieval
candidatos.autores: Vicente Balmaseda, Dongqi Fu, Jiarui Feng, Ren chen, Hanqing Zeng, Tianxin Wei

On the one hand, Semantic IDs (SIDs) give discrete models shared parameters and pretrained semantic structure, but discretizing items into hard codes discards some information from the original content embeddings. candidatos.titulo: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization
candidatos.autores: Riccardo Maggioni
candidatos.resumo: Time-series interpretation often requires both numerical observations and textual context. Integrating these inputs into a pretrained language model raises a representation question: how should a signal enter the model's token sequence? We present TEMPO, which extends an LLM's vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization. candidatos.titulo: Modular and Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search with Vectorium and kANNolo
candidatos.autores: Silvio Martinico, Franco Maria Nardini, Cosimo Rulli, Rossano Venturini
candidatos.resumo: Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search over neural embeddings powers modern retrieval systems such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Embeddings come in three representations (dense, sparse and multi-vector), and efficient search combines an index structure, a similarity function and a quantization scheme. candidatos.titulo: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding
candidatos.autores: Yang Hu, Duo Wang, Ning Li, Kang Li, Junda She, Chengcheng Guo
candidatos.resumo: Generative recommendation has been widely adopted in large-scale industrial recommendation systems, where multimodal item embeddings are quantized into offline semantic identifiers (SIDs) and items are retrieved by autoregressively generating their SIDs. candidatos.titulo: SANAI: Secure ECC Distributed Keyed Parity Embedded in Weights for Protecting Neural Networks against Bit-Flip Attacks
candidatos.autores: Habibur Rahaman, Daniel Lobo, Md Rezoan Ferdous, Swarup Bhunia

candidatos.titulo: Context-Shielded Backdoor Attack against Large Vision-Language Models
candidatos.autores: Zhifang Zhang, Qiang Huang, Chenpeng Wang, Weitong Chen, Olaf Maennel, Wei Emma Zhang

Existing LVLM backdoors fire whenever a triggered image appears, whereas prior deployment-triggered attacks activate only when model weights are quantized or pruned. candidatos.autores: Stepan Zharkov, Krish Singal, Ashwin Padaki, Alexandr Andoni
candidatos.resumo: Sparse attention mechanisms estimate attention over $n$ tokens using a small subset of keys. candidatos.titulo: Index-Free Dynamic Edge Retrieval with Energy-Tail-Aware Partial Scans
candidatos.autores: Mohammad Arif Rasyidi, Omar Alhussein

For edge retrieval, the challenge is to achieve high recall and fast queries without making updates expensive. candidatos.titulo: Time-Decayed Vector Search in the Rhythm of TANGO: Jointly Modeling Semantic Similarity and Temporal Freshness
candidatos.autores: Jiuqi Wei, Qiyao Luo, Quanqing Xu, Chuanhui Yang, Themis Palpanas

However, in a growing range of applications, relevance may evolve over time, making temporal freshness an additional signal beyond semantic similarity. candidatos.titulo: RSLM: Training-Free Vector Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
candidatos.autores: Rastislav Lenhardt, Teodora Dobos, Thomas Vecchiato, Jiri Isa, Igor Ginzburg

candidatos.titulo: Fast and Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search for High-Dimensional LLM Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Nico Hezel, Kai Uwe Barthel, Bruno Schilling, Konstantin Schall, Andre Moelle, Klaus Jung

candidatos.titulo: Accelerating LLM Inference via Vector Index Based Output Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Martin Loretz, Sepp Hochreiter
candidatos.resumo: Large output embedding matrices create a significant memory bandwidth bottleneck during autoregressive decoding, especially for compact LLMs with large multilingual vocabularies. We reformulate the output projection followed by top-k token selection as a maximum inner product search over token embeddings and replace the dense vocabulary projection with an HNSW-based vector index. candidatos.titulo: Amortized Maximum Inner Product Search with Learned Support Functions
candidatos.autores: Theo X. Olausson, João Monteiro, Michal Klein, Marco Cuturi
candidatos.resumo: Maximum inner product search (MIPS) is a crucial subroutine in machine learning, requiring the identification of a vector taken within a database (the keys) that best aligns with a given query. We propose amortized MIPS: a regression-based approach that trains neural networks to directly predict MIPS solutions, amortizing the cost of repeatedly solving MIPS for queries drawn from a known distribution over a fixed key database. Our key insight is that the MIPS value function is the \emph{support} function of the set of keys, a well-studied convex function whose gradient yields the optimal key.

candidatos.autores: Han Chen, Steven Zhu, Yingrui Li

We introduce STARS, a transformer-based sequential recommendation framework built for large-scale, low-latency ecommerce settings. candidatos.autores: Diego Ortego, Marlon Rodríguez, Mario Almagro, Kunal Dahiya, David Jiménez, Juan C. SanMiguel

candidatos.autores: Ruoxuan Li, Xiaoyao Zhong, Jiabao Jin, Peng Cheng, Wangze Ni, Zhitao Shen
candidatos.resumo: Sparse vector Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is crucial in multi-path retrieval for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Recent inverted index-based and graph-based algorithms have achieved high search accuracy with practical efficiency. However, their performance in production environments is often limited by redundant distance computations and frequent random memory accesses. candidatos.titulo: VIBE: Vector Index Benchmark for Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Elias Jääsaari, Ville Hyvönen, Matteo Ceccarello, Teemu Roos, Martin Aumüller
candidatos.resumo: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search is a performance-critical component of many machine learning pipelines, and rigorous benchmarking is essential for assessing the performance of vector indexes for ANN search. However, the datasets of existing benchmarks no longer represent modern ANN applications, creating a need for an up-to-date benchmark. candidatos.titulo: Stitching Inner Product and Euclidean Metrics for Topology-aware Maximum Inner Product Search
candidatos.autores: Tingyang Chen, Cong Fu, Xiangyu Ke, Yunjun Gao, Yabo Ni, Anxiang Zeng
candidatos.resumo: Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is a fundamental challenge in machine learning and information retrieval, particularly in high-dimensional data applications. Existing approaches to MIPS either rely solely on Inner Product (IP) similarity, which faces issues with local optima and redundant computations, or reduce the MIPS problem to the Nearest Neighbor Search under the Euclidean metric via space projection, leading to topology destruction and information loss. Despite the divergence of the two paradigms, we argue that there is no inherent binary opposition between IP and Euclidean metrics.

candidatos.autores: Daichi Amagata, Kazuyoshi Aoayama, Keito Kido, Sumio Fujita

candidatos.titulo: Maximum Inner Product is Query-Scaled Nearest Neighbor
candidatos.autores: Tingyang Chen, Cong Fu, Kun Wang, Xiangyu Ke, Yunjun Gao, Wenchao Zhou
candidatos.resumo: Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) for high-dimensional vectors is pivotal across databases, information retrieval, and artificial intelligence. candidatos.autores: Bruce W. Brewer, Haitao Wang

candidatos.autores: Alex Conway, Laxman Dhulipala, Martin Farach-Colton, Ben Landrum, Christopher Musco, Yarin Shechter

candidatos.autores: Majid Daliri, Mohammadreza Daneshvaramoli, Purna Dutta, Edo Liberty, Cameron Musco, Christopher Musco

candidatos.autores: Dongfang Zhao

candidatos.autores: Zhutao Zhuang, Nong Xiao, Zhiguang Chen, Yue Yu

candidatos.autores: Shankar Bhamidi, Souvik Dhara, Lars Schroeder, Clara Stegehuis

candidatos.autores: Qi Lin, Zhenyu Zhang, Jun Kong, Zhichao Cao

Although GPUs offer massive parallelism and high-bandwidth memory for batched vector search, their limited VRAM capacity makes fully GPU-resident billion-scale indexes difficult to deploy. candidatos.titulo: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$

candidatos.resumo: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. candidatos.autores: Pier-Jean Malandrino

candidatos.titulo: EntroPack: Fast and Accurate Entropy-Coded Weight Compression at Arbitrary Bitrates
candidatos.autores: Hong Zhang, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen
candidatos.resumo: Weight compression helps large neural networks fit deployment memory budgets, but common fixed-width formats offer only coarse storage choices. Entropy coding supports finer rates, yet the achieved size depends on the quantized weight distribution and coding overhead. Exploiting this flexibility requires accurate rate selection and efficient weight reconstruction for inference. candidatos.titulo: An Attribute-Based Measure of Video Complexity
candidatos.autores: Aditya Sarkar, Yi Li, Zihao Wang, Hao Yuan, Sai Vidyaranya Nuthalapati, Aashu Singh
candidatos.resumo: A new framework for the estimation of the complexity posed by video-question pairs to video-LLMs, Video Attribute-Based Complexity (VideoABC), is proposed. Video complexity is defined as the probability of failure of a video-LLM for a given video-question pair. VideoABC is a non-parametric complexity measure, using a reference video dataset and a pre-defined vocabulary of video attributes informative of complexity, e.g. the scene complexity or the speed of the video event relevant to the question. candidatos.titulo: Lattice Modulo Sampling
candidatos.autores: Yhonatan Kvich, Yonina C. Eldar

Standard modulo analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) fold the signal component-wise into a square domain, reducing the recovery problem to independent one-dimensional problems. candidatos.autores: Natalie Lang, Maya Simhi, Nir Shlezinger

candidatos.titulo: Scalar Lattices and Probabilistic Shaping for Dithered Wyner-Ziv Quantization

candidatos.titulo: Ultrasonic spin pumping in the antiferromagnetic acoustic resonator $α-\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$

These interactions suggest a dynamic connection between collective excitations of spins, quantized as magnons, and elastic waves generated by perturbations in the crystal lattice, quantized as phonons. candidatos.autores: Iris Kaplan, Or Ordentlich

candidatos.autores: Eric Lei, Hamed Hassani, Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti

candidatos.autores: Shaobin Zhuang, Yuang Ai, Jiaming Han, Xiaohui Li, Huaibo Huang, Xiangyu Yue

candidatos.autores: Daniel Schwartz, Dario Salvucci, Yusuf Osmanlioglu, Richard Vallett, Genevieve Dion, Ali Shokoufandeh

candidatos.autores: Shankar Veludandi, Gulrukh Kurdistan, Uzma Mushtaque

candidatos.autores: Yoshith Roy Kotla, Varshith Roy Kotla

candidatos.autores: Dong Liu, Shu Wang, Yanxuan Yu, Haisheng Wang, Ben Lengerich

candidatos.autores: Sewon Min, Weijia Shi, Mike Lewis, Xilun Chen, Wen-tau Yih, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
